question: What fraction of officially inactive players appear on the NFL injury report at all?
have: Measured on the 8 clubs where every live row was read and joined to the official inactive list: 26 of 46 inactive players (56.5%) do not appear on the injury report in any form. Excluding the two emergency third quarterbacks, 24 of 44 (54.5%).
missing: The other 16 clubs of Week 10, and every prior week.
clears: The same join computed for all 32 clubs and at least one full season, with the denominator published and the emergency-third-QB rows separated out.

question: What does 'Questionable' mean empirically?
have: On the 8 joined clubs, 4 of 26 players carrying a Questionable designation were inactive (15.4%).
missing: A usable sample. n = 26 in one week is far too small, and one club (LV) went 2 for 2.
clears: Several seasons of designations joined to the official inactive lists, with a confidence interval and a club-clustered standard error.

question: What does 'Doubtful' mean empirically?
have: 1 of 4 Doubtful players on the joined clubs was inactive (25%).
missing: n = 4. The brief asks for a calibrated probability with a confidence interval; this cannot support one.
clears: n >= 200 Doubtful designations joined to inactive lists across seasons.

question: Does an 'Out' designation guarantee the player is inactive?
have: No, and the official reserve list explains most of it. Of 17 Out players on the joined clubs, 14 were inactive and 2 more were placed on the official reserve list during the week (TreVeyon Henderson, NE, 11/14; Tyler Goodson, DAL, 11/14). 16 of 17 (94.1%) are therefore explained by two official pages. Kerby Joseph (DET) is the one case neither page explains.
missing: An explanation for Kerby Joseph: Out on the injury report, absent from the Week 10 inactive list, and absent from the November 2026 reserve list.
clears: The reserve list captured as a dated field of the weekly snapshot, so an Out player who went on IR is separated from an Out player who was expected to be inactive.
status: answered for 16 of 17; one case flagged (F3)

question: Which players are on a reserve list and therefore absent from the weekly report?
have: The league publishes it. https://www.nfl.com/transactions/league/reserve-list/2026/11 lists 25 Reserve/Injured moves for November 2026, each dated and club-indexed. It includes Malik Willis (MIA, 11/10) - the exact case the project brief cites as the reason a reserve list is needed - and it explains two of the three Out players who were missing from the inactive list.
missing: Nothing for this month. The gap is that the reserve list is not captured: nothing in this repository ingests it, so a player on IR still looks simply absent.
clears: Add the reserve list to the scheduled capture as a dated field, and join it to the weekly injury and inactive captures.
status: answered - the official page exists and was read

question: Does the league publish depth charts?
have: No. https://www.nfl.com/teams/baltimore-ravens/depth-chart returns the official 404 page, and the club page's only sections are Info, Roster and Stats.
missing: Nothing - this one is settled for nfl.com. The open part is whether the 32 club domains publish them in a parseable form.
clears: A club-by-club read of all 32 official club sites, each with a URL, a date and a parser that survives the 'published as an image' failure mode.
status: answered for nfl.com; open for the 32 club sites
